The aim of the present paper is to provide a global presentation of the theory of special Finsler manifolds. We introduce and investigate globally (or intrinsically, free from local coordinates) many of the most important and most commonly used special Finsler manifolds: locally Minkowskian, Berwald, Landesberg, general Landesberg, $P$-reducible, $C$-reducible, semi-$C$-reducible, quasi-$C$-reducible, $P^{*}$-Finsler, $C^{h}$-recurrent, $C^{v}$-recurrent, $C^{0}$-recurrent, $S^{v}$-recurrent, $S^{v}$-recurrent of the second order, $C_{2}$-like, $S_{3}$-like, $S_{4}$-like, $P_{2}$-like, $R_{3}$-like, $P$-symmetric, $h$-isotropic, of scalar curvature, of constant curvature, of $p$-scalar curvature, of $s$-$ps$-curvature. The global definitions of these special Finsler manifolds are introduced. Various relationships between the different types of the considered special Finsler manifolds are found. Many local results, known in the literature, are proved globally and several new results are obtained. As a by-product, interesting identities and properties concerning the torsion tensor fields and the curvature tensor fields are deduced. Although our investigation is entirely global, we provide; for comparison reasons, an appendix presenting a local counterpart of our global approach and the local definitions of the special Finsler spaces considered.

From a global—or intrinsic—perspective, it defines and studies many of the principal classes commonly encountered in Finsler geometry: locally Minkowskian, Berwald, Landesberg, general Landesberg, \(P\)-reducible, \(C\)-reducible, semi-\(C\)-reducible, quasi-\(C\)-reducible, \(P^{*}\)-Finsler, \(C^{h}\)-recurrent, \(C^{v}\)-recurrent, \(C^{0}\)-recurrent, \(S^{v}\)-recurrent, second-order \(S^{v}\)-recurrent, \(C_{2}\)-like, \(S_{3}\)-like, \(S_{4}\)-like, \(P_{2}\)-like, \(R_{3}\)-like, \(P\)-symmetric, \(h\)-isotropic, scalar-curvature, constant-curvature, \(p\)-scalar-curvature, and \(s\)-\(ps\)-curvature manifolds.

outputs.L5:
### The Finsler–Minkowskian Perspective

Finsler geometry generalizes Riemannian geometry by allowing the length of a tangent vector to depend on both its magnitude and direction. At each point of a Finsler manifold, the tangent space is equipped with a Minkowskian norm rather than an inner product. This norm may be anisotropic, meaning that movement in different directions can have different geometric costs.

The Minkowskian structure provides the local model for Finsler geometry, much as Euclidean space provides the local model for Riemannian geometry. By varying these norms smoothly from point to point, one obtains a rich framework for studying geodesics, curvature, optimization, and physical systems in which direction-dependent behavior is important.

Working intrinsically on the slit tangent bundle and its pullback bundles, we formulate the relevant connections, curvature tensors, sprays, and nonlinear connection data without recourse to local coordinates. Within this setting, major classes—including Riemannian, locally Minkowski, Berwald, Landsberg, Douglas, and projectively flat Finsler manifolds—are characterized by invariant tensorial conditions. We establish implication diagrams and equivalence criteria linking these classes, clarify the roles of torsion, curvature, holonomy, and projective invariants, and identify the hypotheses under which local characterizations extend globally. The framework also separates genuinely global phenomena from artifacts of coordinate calculations and provides natural tools for analyzing morphisms, geodesic equivalence, and rigidity. Classical results are recovered as immediate consequences, while several relationships admit streamlined intrinsic proofs and extensions to broader geometric settings. This unified approach offers a systematic basis for the classification and comparison of special Finsler structures.
